source_id_policy: Source IDs are fixed for this stage and must not be silently rebound. The draft cites these IDs and the index records exact source URLs.
evidence_limits: Public primary documentation, public source code and public released issue/fix history only. Research retrieval is not product validation. No downloaded code was run.

claim_source_comparison.claim: Weekly rehearsal should remain at the venue's local wall-clock time across DST; a zoned DTSTART + recurring rule communicates this, and a VTIMEZONE definition must cover the season.
claim_source_comparison.operation_subject: iCalendar recurrence expansion in RFC 5545; Google Calendar API v3 start.timeZone field.
claim_source_comparison.conditions: TZID/VTIMEZONE are paired; local date-time without TZID is floating; TZID DTSTART requires UNTIL in UTC; client support still varies. Google Help additionally warns about future/past events and DST-rule updates.
claim_source_comparison.applicability_limit: Normative format/API behavior, not observed client implementation or refresh result.

claim_source_comparison.claim: Keep one UID for the recurring series; use original recurrence identity for a moved instance and exclude a canceled instance from the recurrence set.
claim_source_comparison.operation_subject: iCalendar event series/exception; Google API get/update of a single recurring event instance.
claim_source_comparison.conditions: RECURRENCE-ID is original scheduled time; Google originalStartTime is immutable; Google API status=cancelled only for a specific instance; exact feed serialization still to test.
claim_source_comparison.applicability_limit: Standards/API identity, not guarantee across all clients.

claim_source_comparison.claim: A file import is a snapshot; URL subscription refresh is client/service controlled and cannot be promised immediate.
claim_source_comparison.operation_subject: Google Calendar computer import vs public-URL add; Outlook.com web upload vs Subscribe from web.
claim_source_comparison.conditions: Google source must be public for URL add; Outlook documentation says refresh can exceed 24 hours despite approximate 3-hour guidance; numeric builds unavailable.
claim_source_comparison.applicability_limit: Exact documented web operations only; actual refresh must be measured per target app/version.

claim_source_comparison.claim: The Nextcloud 35 weekly user-app subscription interval and one-day server-cached subscription default describe different operations.
claim_source_comparison.operation_subject: Nextcloud Calendar app subscribing to a feed vs Nextcloud server periodically refreshing its own cached upstream subscription.
claim_source_comparison.conditions: Nextcloud 35 user manual says weekly default; Nextcloud 35 admin manual says one-day server default absent a source refresh interval. The docs appear to concern internal feed subscriptions but do not reconcile the default; treat as an unresolved documentation conflict, not separate proven defaults.
claim_source_comparison.applicability_limit: Neither page sets refresh behavior of Google, Outlook, Apple or other external clients fetching a Nextcloud public URL.

claim_source_comparison.claim: Keep policy reminders out of the feed and test per-member local reminder behavior.
claim_source_comparison.operation_subject: iCalendar VALARM and client subscription settings / Google API per-user reminders.
claim_source_comparison.conditions: Apple Mac allows Ignore alerts; Google API describes reminders for authenticated user; Nextcloud app notifications apply to owner/write-sharees, while third-party sync may show notices.
claim_source_comparison.applicability_limit: No uniform reminder promise established for every subscribed-feed client.

claim_source_comparison.claim: One-occurrence property edits can lose inherited series fields in at least one historical remote-calendar client path; test room-only overrides.
claim_source_comparison.operation_subject: Thunderbird Lightning 68.2 remote recurrence exception editing and the later source fix.
claim_source_comparison.conditions: Bug report, code change and version history are limited to Thunderbird Calendar; current other clients are not covered.
claim_source_comparison.applicability_limit: Regression example only; no current product validation performed.

sources.title: RFC 5545: iCalendar
sources.released_version_or_commit: IETF Standards Track RFC, September 2009; RFC Editor landing page notes updates by RFCs 5546, 6868, 7529, 7953, 7986, 9073, 9074, 9253.
sources.locator: TZID §3.2.19; DATE-TIME; RRULE/UNTIL; recurrence set; RECURRENCE-ID; UID; EXDATE; STATUS; VALARM (notably pp. 27-28, 112-123).
sources.observed_operation: Reading normative iCalendar serialization/recurrence definitions for a published VEVENT series and its exceptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A DATE-TIME without TZID is floating; TZID refers to VTIMEZONE, with one zone definition per TZID and coverage across recurrence. For DTSTART with a zone reference, RRULE UNTIL is UTC. A recurrence instance uses its original scheduled date/time for RECURRENCE-ID; EXDATE excludes dates. UID plus recurrence identity is stable for series/instance tracking.
sources.applicability: Governs ICS syntax/meaning, not consumer refresh cadence or exact implementation behavior. Product interoperability remains to be validated.

sources.title: RFC 5546: iTIP
sources.locator: §3.2.5 CANCEL; recurring VEVENT cancellation with/without RECURRENCE-ID.
sources.observed_operation: Reading the organizer-to-attendee scheduling-message cancellation operation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CANCEL is an iTIP message sent by the organizer to affected attendees; RECURRENCE-ID identifies one instance. Whole-series cancellation omits RECURRENCE-ID.
sources.applicability: Boundary only: do not conflate attendee cancellation messages with a passive read-only ICS feed update.

sources.title: RFC 4791: CalDAV
sources.locator: §8.2 synchronization, ETag/cache behavior, calendar-query REPORT and calendar object resources.
sources.observed_operation: Reading the client/server calendar data access and synchronization model.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A client that supports sync can cache calendar object URI/ETag and synchronize; server and client must implement the relevant protocol operations.
sources.applicability: Analogous server synchronization route, not a bare URL subscription or downloaded file; often entails accounts and permissions.

sources.title: RFC 6578: WebDAV Collection Synchronization
sources.observed_operation: Reading incremental collection synchronization with DAV:sync-token.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: With a valid token, changed or removed member URLs can be reported; initial sync sends an empty token and retrieves collection members.
sources.applicability: CalDAV/WebDAV server and client must implement the sync extension; not a guarantee for public ICS URL subscribers.

sources.title: Google Calendar public calendar help
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online Google Calendar Help; numeric service version/build not published.
sources.locator: How public calendars work; Mark your calendar as public; Share your public calendar.
sources.observed_operation: Publishing a Google Calendar and retrieving shareable/public/iCal links from desktop web settings.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Calendar must be made public for public iCal address; public calendars may be searchable; owner may hide details by sharing free/busy; Workspace administrator may restrict sharing; visibility change may take up to four hours.
sources.applicability: Applies to Google Calendar's public-hosting route; privacy choice belongs to the owner/manager.

sources.title: Google Calendar subscribe by URL help
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online Google Calendar Help; numeric service version/build not published.
sources.locator: Use a link to add a public calendar; notes on subscription setup by browser vs mobile app.
sources.observed_operation: Adding a published calendar URL under Other calendars in Google Calendar on a computer browser.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The source must be public to add by URL; a new subscription cannot be set up in the Google Calendar mobile apps, though after computer setup it appears in the app.
sources.applicability: Setup behavior only; page states no refresh interval or guarantee.

sources.title: Google Calendar import events help
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online Google Calendar Help; numeric service version/build not published.
sources.locator: Import events into Google Calendar; repeat-event CSV note.
sources.observed_operation: Importing an ICS/CSV file on a computer into a selected Google Calendar.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Imported events do not stay in sync. CSV recurring events may become single events. Default import target is primary calendar unless user selects another.
sources.applicability: Supports a downloadable static snapshot via ICS; import is not live subscription.

sources.title: Google Calendar API v3 Events and recurring event guide
sources.released_version_or_commit: Google Calendar API v3; current reference page, retrieval date 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Event fields start.timeZone, originalStartTime, recurringEventId, status, reminders; recurring events guide: access instances and modify/cancel one instance.
sources.observed_operation: Creating recurring event resource; retrieving an instance; updating its instance URL; cancellation example sets instance status=cancelled.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For recurring event expansion, start.timeZone is required and uses an IANA identifier. originalStartTime remains the instance's original scheduled time if moved. A cancelled recurring exception is an instance-level status; consumer API operations require authorization.
sources.applicability: Versioned API evidence for Google server operations only; not equivalent to public feed import/subscription semantics.

sources.title: Outlook.com import or subscribe help
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Microsoft Support page; applies to Outlook.com/Outlook on the web; numeric client/service build not published.
sources.locator: Subscribe to a calendar; Upload a calendar from a file; difference between importing and subscribing.
sources.observed_operation: Outlook.com Subscribe from web URL vs Upload from file .ics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Subscription refresh may take more than 24 hours although updates should happen approximately every three hours; no maximum is guaranteed. Upload/import is a point-in-time snapshot and never auto-refreshes.
sources.applicability: Exact Outlook.com web operation in current docs; not a guarantee about every Outlook desktop/mobile version or other providers.

sources.title: Apple Calendar subscription guides
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Apple Support guides; numeric iOS/macOS version not stated.
sources.locator: iPhone external read-only calendar subscription; Mac Calendar New Calendar Subscription, Auto-refresh, Ignore alerts.
sources.observed_operation: Subscribing to a URL for an external .ics calendar on iPhone/Mac; configuring Mac subscription refresh and alert display.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Provider controls subscribed events; Mac user may select auto-refresh frequency or ignore alerts. The guide gives no single default refresh interval applying to all Apple clients.
sources.applicability: Supports read-only URL subscription on common Apple clients; specific device release/build and actual refresh schedule require validation.

sources.title: Nextcloud 35 Calendar User Manual
sources.released_version_or_commit: Nextcloud 35 User Manual (stable docs page identified as version 35).
sources.locator: Publishing a calendar; Subscribe to a Calendar; reminders; recurrence; iCalendar file support.
sources.observed_operation: Publishing a read-only external link and retrieving its subscription/export links; subscribing to an external iCal feed within Nextcloud Calendar app.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Public link is read-only to external users and public page offers subscribe/export. The user manual says Nextcloud Calendar app subscriptions refresh weekly by default, subject to administrator configuration.
sources.applicability: Useful alternate publishing host and client. Refresh statement is a Nextcloud app subscription behavior and conflicts with the one-day default in the Nextcloud 35 administration manual; exact default remains unresolved.

sources.title: Nextcloud 35 Calendar Administration Manual
sources.released_version_or_commit: Nextcloud 35 Administration Manual (stable docs page identified as version 35).
sources.observed_operation: Nextcloud server caches calendars that its own users have subscribed to and periodically fetches their source feed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The administration manual says calendar subscriptions are cached on server and refreshed periodically; it honors a source refresh interval and otherwise defaults to one day; administrators can set another DateInterval.
sources.applicability: Likely relates to Nextcloud internal feed subscription/cache behavior, while R11 says weekly by default. Do not resolve the discrepancy without a versioned discriminating check. Does not govern external clients subscribing to Nextcloud public URLs.

sources.title: W3C WebSub
sources.locator: §2 high-level protocol flow; §5 subscription validation/leases; §6 publishing/delivery.
sources.observed_operation: Publisher notifies hub of an updated topic; hub delivers updates to registered subscriber callback URLs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Subscribers require callback endpoints; subscriptions are verified and expire via leases; hubs retry only within their own limits.
sources.applicability: Analogous web pub/sub and possible update-notice channel; no evidence common calendar clients consume event feeds via WebSub.

sources.title: Mozilla Bugzilla 1595332
sources.released_version_or_commit: Affected: Thunderbird 68.2.1 / Lightning 68.2.0 (remote calendar); fixed release tracking: Thunderbird 91, uplift to 91.0b4.
sources.locator: Reproduction and environment; comments diagnosing recurring proxy properties; backout/relanding; Thunderbird 91 status.
sources.observed_operation: Edit one occurrence of a remote recurring event and add a description; reported inherited location lost on save.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report says remote calendar; discussion says broadly remote calendars and local ICS were affected except storage calendar due to a prior fix. First patch was backed out after recurrence tests failed; later patch marked fixed and uplifted.
sources.applicability: Historical Thunderbird recurrence-editor defect, relevant as an example regression test for a room-only instance change. Not evidence of current behavior in other clients.

sources.title: Mozilla changeset 3787e583daf7
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mercurial node 3787e583daf7d3026fa6fcc7bf08da03c4fcfb56; Bug 1595332; final patch; later uplift referenced by R14.
sources.locator: calendar/base/src/calItemBase.js diff; calendar/test/unit/test_items.js tests for recurring event and exception properties, including LOCATION inheritance.
sources.observed_operation: Read immutable source patch and regression tests as text; did not execute downloaded code.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The final change exposes inherited parent properties for recurring proxy/exception objects; test additions assert inherited properties, allowing an explicit exception override. The code and tests are scoped to Thunderbird Calendar internals.
sources.applicability: Primary source for a historical recurrence-property fix and regression test idea; does not predict behavior in other products.

sources.title: Google Calendar Help: Use Google Calendar in different time zones
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online Google Calendar Help; numeric service version/build not published.
sources.locator: How Calendar uses time zones; create/change event with a different time zone; Understand how Calendar handles daylight saving time.
sources.observed_operation: Google Calendar web event time-zone configuration, display for invitees in different zones, and viewing while traveling.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Help says events appear in local time to invitees and the viewer while traveling; it also warns past/future events might not reflect DST changes, dates adjust as time advances within a few years, and zone-rule changes can leave earlier-created events wrong.
sources.applicability: Google Calendar service documentation only; does not establish behavior in Apple, Outlook, Nextcloud or other feed consumers.
